files.alt: Cover: Missed a day? Your habit is fine. Four rules for people who restart every Monday.
files.text: 4 rules for people who restart every Monday Missed a day? Your habit is fine.

files.alt: Rule 1: one missed day is noise, two is a pattern. Never miss twice in a row.
files.text: One missed day is noise. Two is a pattern. 1 Protect one line: never miss twice in a row.

files.alt: Myth: a habit takes 21 days. Fact: 66 days on average in a 2010 study, and missing one day didn't matter.
files.text: A habit takes 21 days 66 days on average. Missing one didn't matter.

files.alt: Rule 2: shrink it on bad days. Do two minutes instead of twenty.
files.text: Shrink it on bad days 2 No time for 20 minutes? Do 2. On a bad day, the rep counts, not the size.

files.alt: Rule 3: count weeks, not days. Six out of seven is a good week.
files.text: Count weeks, not days 3 A streak counter calls 6 out of 7 a failure. Your week calls it a good week.

files.alt: Rule 4: tie the habit to something you already do, like coffee or opening the laptop.
files.text: Tie it to something you already do 4 After coffee. Before email. When the laptop opens. Pick a cue you never skip.

files.alt: Recap of the four rules: never miss twice, shrink it on bad days, count weeks not days, tie it to a cue.
files.text: The 4 rules Never miss twice Shrink it on bad days Count weeks, not days Tie it to a cue

files.alt: Screenshot of plodd's week view: 6 of 7 days done, Wednesday missed.
files.text: plodd counts your week Miss Wednesday. Still a good week.
